# Neg Juliet bracket smuggle

In his own maltese training on rings with the light band, SasaVenos trains rings twice per week with around 10 sets of holds per week, and concludes: do not do more than 20 to 30 reps or 30 to 40 seconds of volume per session. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]

## Details

- He only trains holds in his 80 to 90 percent rep max, which he says is 8 to 16 seconds and 4 to 8 reps. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- He trains rings twice per week, around 10 sets of holds per session, with maltese on the light band. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- His conclusion: use only the rubber band that takes away five to nine kilograms, and do not do more than 20 to 30 reps or 30 to 40 seconds of volume per session. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
- He says this is his opinion. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]

## Evidence

- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "perform movements and isometrics that are in my 80 to 90 percent rep max that is 8 to 16 seconds and 4 to 8 reps and that means that i need to only do maltese with the light band and so i train rings twice per week only around 10 sets of holds [per session]"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "but this is my conclusion change progressions of a skill that's in 80 to 90 percent of your one rep max use only the rubber band that takes away five to nine kilograms don't do more than 20 to 30 reps or 30 to 40 seconds of volume per session"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "i got from 8.5 seconds with band to 11 seconds of body [bodyweight] with maltese hold in just five weeks"
- vid-krqBQjUydGY (SasaVenos): "of course this is my opinion and you're allowed to disagree with me"

## Example From The Source

His maltese hold went from 8.5 seconds with band to 11 seconds of body [bodyweight] with maltese hold in just five weeks. [src: vid-krqBQjUydGY]
